svg.title: Graft-bed contact and quilting
svg.desc: Fluid or shear separating a graft from its recipient bed threatens incorporation. Fixation brings the graft into close apposition and limits dead space. Rat imbibition evidence supports a mechanism, not a human clinical success rate; bed vascularity, infection and graft handling also matter. View: Generic free-graft interface, conceptual section. Scale: Conceptual schematic; not to scale. Units: No measured geometry; any dimensions are illustrative. Clinical review pending; no named clinician has signed off. Concept sources: Fukui et al.: plasmatic imbibition in rat grafts (1992 animal experiment), https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1535840/; access: abstract checked; Mechanistic graft-bed exchange in a rat musculocutaneous model; clinical graft take is not guaranteed by quilting. Barbagli: bulbar urethroplasty using the dorsal approach (2003 technical article), https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15745501/; access: abstract checked; Dorsal graft placement on the corporal tunical bed; no survey preference percentage used. WARWIKI original vector schematic; individual illustrator not recorded. No separate figure reuse license recorded; linked sources are concept references, not artwork licenses.

svg.text: The quilting stitch — why graft-bed contact matters
an initially avascular free graft needs contact with a suitable bed during imbibition → inosculation → neovascularization
plasma + new vessels reach the graft
